question: Does trying to answer questions on a topic before studying it, and getting them wrong, waste time?
answer: No, it helps. Richland, Kornell and Kao gave students questions on a passage before they read it; most answers were wrong, yet those students later remembered the tested material better than students who spent the same time just reading. A wrong guess makes the right answer land somewhere ready for it.
move: Guess before you learn; the wrong guess makes room for the answer.
ask: Before I next read up on something, could I first write down what I think the answers are?
source: Richland, Kornell and Kao, JEP: Applied, 2009
reference: Richland, Kornell and Kao, The Pretesting Effect: Do Unsuccessful Retrieval Attempts Enhance Learning?, Journal of Experimental Psychology: Applied, 2009
